risks: Large-load growth requires regulatory approvals and substantial capital while financing costs are rising.
Higher debt and interest expense can dilute benefits from rate-base growth; regulatory outcomes determine recovery timing and returns.
The causal bridge from announced large loads to durable earnings remains approval- and construction-dependent.
Debt-funded capital growth can be value-dilutive if regulatory recovery lags financing costs or projects are delayed.
Wildfire liability is asymmetric because extreme outcomes may exceed insurance and mitigation cannot reduce ignition probability to zero.
Large-load customers can improve utilization but create concentration and build-ahead risk if expected demand is delayed or cancelled.
unknowns: Timing and realized economics of data-center load additions and associated generation buildout remain prospective.

Upper-bound Smokehouse Creek liability remains not reasonably estimable.

contradictions: Infrastructure recovery is lifting earnings while the debt used to fund expansion is simultaneously increasing financing costs.
Demand growth strengthens the need for infrastructure while simultaneously increasing capital, financing and reliability obligations.

Infrastructure recovery is lifting earnings while debt, interest expense and equity financing simultaneously consume part of that benefit; both effects are presently observable and should remain separate.
